newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae CEO to announce resignation - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae CEO to announce resignation - WSJ.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association Chief Executive Lawrence Hough is expected to announce plans to resign after shareholders vote this summer on a reorganization and privatization plan, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said Hough is likely to announce his plans later today.
Officials at the company, also known as Sallie Mae, also said they plan to give a group of dissident directors five of the 15 board seats if current management wins the vote.
Sallie Mae management also is expected to announce that its choice for chairman is David Vitale, vice chairman of First Chicago NBD Corp.

It is hoped that Hough's resignation, along with a promise for a third of the board's seats, will persuade a majority of shareholders to back management at a special shareholders meeting in late July or August, the Journal said.
"We have not been able to break the deadlock," Hough told the Journal.
Hough said his decision to resign is partly a response to concerns among shareholders about becoming private company as well as his belief that "overall change begins at the top."
